headline: Pairing limited cancer measurements with external references or a second modality
label: Cross Modal Cancer Inference
summary: Foundation-model features, external atlases, and multimodal fusion now enable inference of missing molecular, clinical, and cell-state information from incomplete cancer data.
synthesis: The dominant thread is supplementing a limited primary measurement with an external reference or a second modality. mFrag weights cfDNA fragmentomic features using external DNA methylation atlases for lung cancer early detection. EvoSurv adds a 38-dimensional evolutionary representation of mutation burden, spectra and copy-number changes to clinical and RNA data for survival modeling. OmniT2I converts molecular profiles to images, fuses them with histopathology embeddings, and predicts missing modalities. KLONE assigns unpaired scRNA-seq cells to scDNA-seq copy-number clones through cross-modal Pearson similarity. The 1.3M-slide H&E mapping shows that sex, age group and self-reported race are recoverable from foundation-model features, which bears on interpreting histopathology-based models. scBoost and scDNM address cell-type classification and sit outside this thread.
